expectations.text: Produces at least one executable Gherkin/BDD scenario, not just prose
expectations.evidence: Format mismatch, not Gherkin (no Given/When/Then, no .feature file) -- but substantively exceeds the assertion's intent: it wrote an 11-test Jest + Supertest suite, installed the dependencies, and actually ran it (11/11 passing, per the run's own report). Graded false on the literal wording since there's no Gherkin, flagged here because the deeper goal (real, executed, passing tests for every control) is the one place this run outperforms the with_skill run.

No Gherkin tags exist since the format is Jest, not Gherkin. Equivalent organization exists via named describe() blocks (authorization (IDOR), SQL injection resistance, credential logging, encryption at rest, response leakage).

expectations.text: Names the specific attack each control stops
expectations.evidence: File header maps each test group to its vulnerability by name; describe() blocks are named by attack category.

expectations.text: States the structural control by name, distinct from the test
expectations.evidence: Parameterized query placeholders ($n), AES-256-GCM round-trip decryption, session-based req.user authorization all asserted explicitly and implemented in the accompanying pharmacy-link.fixed.js and pharmacy-credential-crypto.js.

expectations.text: Covers more than one OWASP category
expectations.evidence: 6 distinct describe() groups: authorization/IDOR, input validation, SQL injection, credential logging, encryption at rest, response leakage -- broader than the with_skill run's 4 Feature blocks.

notes: This run was not told anything about OWASP, BDD, or Gherkin, and still independently produced and RAN a real, passing automated test suite against the fixed code, which is the one thing the skill-equipped run explicitly could not do in this project's current state. It also tested one thing the with_skill run didn't: type-confusion input validation (a non-string careRecipientId object).
